web.remuxWizard.help.mode.Simple.text: Combines the selected tracks as they are. In Synchronization you set the audio and subtitle delays in milliseconds.
web.remuxWizard.help.mode.DelayCorrectio: FrameSync compares the frames of the two versions, finds the constant delay, verifies it and applies it to audio and subtitles. If one version is PAL and the other NTSC, choose the speed correction in Synchronization: RemuxForge verifies it and finds the delay with the stretch applied. For versions with cuts or different scenes use Edit alignment.
web.remuxWizard.help.mode.DeepAnalysis.t: Deep Analysis compares the two versions scene by scene, finds cuts and added or removed scenes and rebuilds the alignment of audio and subtitles. It also accepts speed correction for PAL/NTSC versions. Imported audio is always converted: in Processing choose the format and what to process.

web.remux.help.preset.title: Preset
web.remux.help.preset.text: A preset reapplies in one click the mux type and the settings you use often. Load replaces the current settings, Delete removes the preset from the list. Paths and overwrite stay as set for the open job.
web.remux.help.tracks.title: Track selection
web.remux.help.tracks.text: By rules picks tracks by language and codec, and it is the mode presets save. Advanced selection shows every track in the batch and lets you choose one by one which to keep and which to import.
web.remux.help.source.title: Source file or folder
web.remux.help.source.text: The version to keep as the base: the video and the tracks you want to keep come from here. Choose a folder for a whole season or a single file.
web.remux.help.language.title: Lang file or folder
web.remux.help.language.text: The version to import audio and subtitles from, for example the dub. Left empty, RemuxForge looks for these files in the Source folder.
web.remux.help.target.title: Languages to import
web.remux.help.target.text: The audio and subtitle languages to take from the Lang file. Search by name or code, for example Italian or ita.
web.remux.help.keepAudio.title: Audio languages to keep
web.remux.help.keepAudio.text: The Source audio languages to keep in the result. Empty keeps them all.
web.remux.help.keepSub.title: Subtitle languages to keep
web.remux.help.keepSub.text: The Source subtitle languages to keep in the result. Empty keeps them all.
web.remux.help.audioFormat.title: Audio format
web.remux.help.audioFormat.text: The format of the processed tracks. FLAC and LPCM keep the original quality; AAC, Opus and AC3 take less space.
web.remux.help.audioScope.title: Process audio
web.remux.help.audioScope.text: Chooses which audio to convert: none, only the audio imported from Lang, or all of it including the Source audio. Edit alignment, speed correction and gap filling work on the audio, so they require Lang only or All.
web.remux.validation.audioFormatRequired: Select the audio format required for this configuration.
web.remux.validation.audioScopeRequired: Select Lang or All as the audio processing scope.
web.remux.help.audioSourceFillLang.title: Source audio language
web.remux.help.audioSourceFillLang.text: The Source audio track to take the missing parts from.
web.remux.help.audioDelay.title: Audio delay
web.remux.help.audioDelay.text: Shifts the imported audio: a positive value delays it, a negative one advances it, in milliseconds.
web.remux.help.subDelay.title: Subtitle delay
web.remux.help.subDelay.text: Shifts the imported subtitles: a positive value delays them, a negative one advances them, in milliseconds.
web.remux.help.subCanvas.title: Adapt subtitle canvas
web.remux.help.subCanvas.text: Adapts the position and size of imported subtitles to the Source video, useful when the two versions have different resolution or black bars.
web.remux.help.copyLangChapters.title: Copy chapters from Lang
web.remux.help.copyLangChapters.text: Uses the chapters of the Lang file instead of the Source ones, shifted with the same sync as the imported subtitles.
web.remux.help.errors.title: To fix
web.remux.help.errors.text: These items prevent confirming. Edit takes you straight to the field to correct.
web.remux.help.tools.title: External tools
web.remux.help.tools.text: RemuxForge uses MKVToolNix, FFmpeg and MediaInfo. Paths are set in Settings.
cli.help: Remux mode imports audio tracks and subtitles from MKV files in different languages.
Split mode cuts MKV files into segments or episodes.
Metadata mode applies a metadata preset to MKV files.
--lang en|it                  CLI/UI language for this run
-ext, --extensions <list>      File extensions to scan. Default: mkv
-t,   --target-language <code> ISO 639-2 language code(s), e.g. ita or eng,ita
-l,   --language <path>        Folder with MKV files to import tracks from
If omitted, the source folder is used
-fs,  --framesync              Visual frame comparison for constant delay
-da,  --deep-analysis          dHash pipeline; imported audio requires format and lang/all scope
--speed-correction <m>   off or manual; materializes audio stretch with FFmpeg
--subtitle-canvas-rewrite Rewrite imported PGS, ASS/SSA, VobSub geometry
--copy-lang-chapters     Replace source chapters with the language file's, retimed
--audio-format <fmt>     flac, lpcm, aac, opus, ac3; required for Speed/Deep audio
--audio-scope <scope>    disabled, lang, all; Speed/Deep require lang or all
--audio-gain-db <dB>     Fixed gain, -12 to +12 dB; excludes peak normalization
--output-template <tpl>   Output name template, no extension ({{source}} {{n}} {{episode}} {{chapter}} {{start}} {{end}} {{duration}}, padding :02)
--chapters-per-episode <k>  Group chapters into blocks of k
--snap off|before|after|nearest  (default: nearest, aligns to keyframe and avoids re-encoding)
Common: ita, eng, jpn, ger/deu, fra/fre, spa, por, rus, chi/zho, kor

web.metadata.presetDialog.help.default.t: Define IF/THEN rules evaluated in order. Each rule works on the result produced by previous rules.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.preset.te: Select a preset saved in the RemuxForge configuration folder or create a new one. The path is managed by RemuxForge.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.presetNam: Name used to save the JSON file in the RemuxForge preset folder. It only identifies the preset.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.ruleDescr: Required field. It should describe what the rule does because it is the readable identifier in the pipeline.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.ruleEnabl: Temporarily disables the rule, which stays saved in the preset.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.advancedF: Also shows less common editable fields.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.scope.tex: Chooses where the rule is applied: Matroska container, video tracks, audio tracks, or subtitle tracks. Conditions and editable fields depend on this value.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.condition: Field read from the current pipeline state. After actions run, later rules see updated values; conditions in the same rule are evaluated before its actions.
Comparison applied to the selected field: equality, contains, regex, range, presence, or numeric comparison.
Literal value or template. You can insert tokens from the browser, for example [audio_language], [video_width], or function expressions.
Unit used to normalize numeric comparisons, sizes, and durations.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.trackComp: Compares the current track field with other tracks in the selected group, for example largest or rank 1.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.trackGrou: Defines which other tracks participate in the comparison: same language, same format, same type, or equivalent combinations.
Counts tracks in the selected group and compares that number with the entered value.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.operation: Chooses the action run when conditions are true: set or clear fields and tags, manage statistics tags, set exclusive flags, or remove a track.
Editable field for the action scope. Set and Clear always act on the field selected from this list.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.exclusive: When setting an exclusive flag, other tracks in the same group are updated consistently.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.operation: Template applied to the selected field. Supports tokens like [file_stem] and functions like {[file_name]:TrimEnd(4)}.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.tagTarget: Current follows the rule scope; File applies the tag to the container; Current track applies it to the evaluated track; All tracks applies it to every kept track.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.tagKey.te: Tag key chosen from the UI list.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.clearTags: Requires explicit confirmation before clearing managed tags. A new operation uses the current rule target; an imported preset can specify File, Current track, or All tracks.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.attachmen: Name the attachment takes inside the MKV. Leave it empty when attaching a file and the source file name is used. The cover convention is cover.jpg or cover.png.
Path of the file to attach. It may contain expressions, so the cover can differ per file.
MIME type of the attachment. Leave it empty to derive it from the name extension.
What the tag refers to: 50 the episode or movie, 60 the season, 70 the series. In Matroska the season is PART_NUMBER at level 60 and the episode is PART_NUMBER at level 50. When missing, the level is 50.

web.remux.help.recursive.text: Also looks for files in subfolders, handy for series organized by season.
web.remux.help.extensions.title: Extensions
web.remux.help.extensions.text: The file types to look for, separated by commas. Usually mkv is enough.
web.remux.help.match.title: Matching pattern
web.remux.help.match.text: Recognizes the episode in the file name and pairs Source and Lang files with the same episode. The default recognizes names like S01E05.
web.remux.help.audioCodec.title: Audio codec
web.remux.help.audioCodec.text: Imports only Lang audio with these codecs, for example E-AC-3 or DTS-HD MA. Empty imports every codec of the chosen languages.
web.remux.help.subOnly.title: Subtitles only
web.remux.help.subOnly.text: Imports only subtitles from the Lang file.
web.remux.help.audioOnly.title: Audio only
web.remux.help.audioOnly.text: Imports only audio from the Lang file.
web.remux.help.keepCodec.title: Audio codecs to keep
web.remux.help.keepCodec.text: Keeps only Source audio with these codecs. Empty keeps every codec.
web.remux.help.speed.title: Speed correction
web.remux.help.speed.text: Use it when one version is PAL and the other NTSC, for example 25 versus 23.976 frames per second. Choose the conversion: RemuxForge verifies it, adapts the audio length and finds the delay.
web.remux.help.cropSource.title: Source crop
web.remux.help.cropSource.text: Pixels to ignore at the edges of the Source video while comparing frames, for example black bars or logos. With every value at 0 RemuxForge detects the edges on its own.
web.remux.help.cropLang.title: Lang crop
web.remux.help.cropLang.text: Pixels to ignore at the edges of the Lang video while comparing frames. With every value at 0 RemuxForge detects the edges on its own.
web.remux.help.audio24.title: Reduce from 24 to 16 bit
web.remux.help.audio24.text: Brings the processed audio to 16 bit with high-quality resampling, for lighter files.
web.remux.help.audioGain.title: Volume
web.remux.help.audioGain.text: Adjusts the volume of the processed audio: normalization brings the peak to a chosen value, fixed gain raises or lowers everything by the same amount.
web.remux.help.audioNormalize.title: Peak target
web.remux.help.audioNormalize.text: The level of the highest peak after normalization, from -60 to 0 dB. -1 dB is a safe value.
web.remux.help.audioFixedGain.title: Fixed gain
web.remux.help.audioFixedGain.text: Raises or lowers the volume of all processed audio, from -12 to +12 dB.
web.remux.help.audioSourceFill.title: Fill gaps with Source audio
web.remux.help.audioSourceFill.text: When the imported audio is missing a part, it completes it with the audio of the same scene taken from the Source, so the result has no silences.
The minimum length of a gap, in milliseconds, for it to be filled.
web.remux.help.audioSourceFillGain.title: Fill volume
web.remux.help.audioSourceFillGain.text: Adjusts the volume of the parts taken from the Source, from -12 to +12 dB, to match the imported audio.
web.remux.help.audioSourceFillStart.text: Fills the beginning when the imported audio starts after the video.
web.remux.help.audioSourceFillEnd.title: End
web.remux.help.audioSourceFillEnd.text: Fills the end when the imported audio ends before the video.
web.remux.help.audioSourceFillInsert.tex: Fills the silences the alignment inserts where the Source has extra scenes.
web.remux.help.encoding.title: Video encoding
web.remux.help.encoding.text: Re-encodes the video with a profile, for example to save space. Without a profile the video stays the original.
web.remux.help.destination.title: Destination folder
web.remux.help.destination.text: The folder where RemuxForge writes the resulting files.
web.remux.help.overwrite.title: Overwrite source
web.remux.help.overwrite.text: Writes the result in place of the Source file, without making copies.
web.remux.skip.noEpisodeId: Episode not recognized in the name
web.remux.destinationOverwrite: With overwrite, the results replace the Source files.
web.editMap.noOperations: The EditMap contains no operations. Add a Cut or an Insert from the timeline or the commands above.
web.editMap.timestampHint: Type the time as ss, mm:ss or hh:mm:ss, with milliseconds after a comma or a dot (e.g. 1:30.250).
web.editMap.frameNumberHint: Type a frame number from 1 to {0}.
web.editMap.durationHint: Type a duration in milliseconds greater than zero.
web.editMap.gainHint: Type a value in dB, with a comma or a dot (e.g. -3.5).
web.editMap.noMatchingLanguageFrame: This Source point needs a matching Language frame.
web.splitWizard.title: Configure split
web.splitWizard.note.folderOnly: Available when the source is a folder.
web.splitWizard.help.source: Choose an MKV file or a folder. With a folder, every MKV found is split with the same rules.
web.splitWizard.help.recursive: Also looks for files in the subfolders of the source.
web.splitWizard.help.extensions: File types to look for in the folder, separated by commas. Example: mkv
web.splitWizard.help.mode: Choose how each file is divided. Hover a card to read its description.
web.splitWizard.help.chaptersPerEpisode: Number of chapters that make up one episode. The file is divided into blocks of this size; with 1 you get one file per chapter. When the chapters do not divide evenly, the last episode collects the remaining ones and the plan points it out.
web.splitWizard.help.pattern: One row per episode, with the number of chapters it contains, in order. Example: 5, 5, 5, 6. The total matches the number of chapters in the file.
web.splitWizard.help.ranges: One row for each file to create, with start and end. Write times as 21:40 or 00:21:40, or a frame as f1234. Use END to reach the end of the file.
web.splitWizard.help.splitAt: One row for each point where the file is cut. Two points give three files. Write times as 21:40 or 00:21:40, or a frame as f1234.
web.splitWizard.help.trimStart: Point where the created file begins. Leave it empty to start from the beginning. Write the time as 1:30 or 00:01:30, or a frame as f1234.
web.splitWizard.help.trimEnd: Point where the created file ends. Leave it empty to reach the end. Write the time as 1:30 or 00:01:30, or a frame as f1234.
web.splitWizard.help.snap: With a keyframe, the cut moves to the best point near the one you set and the video is copied as it is, in seconds. "Frame exact" cuts exactly where you set it and re-encodes the start of each part, which takes much longer. Two adjacent parts always share the same boundary.
web.splitWizard.help.template: Name of the created files. Leave it empty to use the scheme shown in the field.
The .mkv extension is added automatically; a slash / creates a subfolder.
{episode}  episode number, from the "Start numbering at" value
{chapter}  name of the first chapter of the part
With :02 the number always has two digits, for example {episode:02}.
web.splitWizard.help.startNumber: First number assigned to {episode}. Useful when a disc continues a series: with 13 the first episode becomes E13 and the next ones follow.
web.splitWizard.help.namePreview: Shows the names the scheme produces for three sample parts. The final names appear in the plan of each file.
web.splitWizard.help.outputDir: Folder where the created files are saved. Leave it empty to save them next to each source file.
web.splitWizard.help.force: On: files with the same name are replaced. Off: they are kept as they are and their creation is skipped. The same choice also applies to Join parts.
web.splitWizard.help.errors: Each entry points to a field to fix. Press Edit to reach it; the entry disappears as soon as the field is correct.
web.splitWizard.help.summary: Check your choices and press Prepare and review: the files are found and a cut plan is prepared for each one. When a plan needs attention the review opens, otherwise you go straight to the file list. Files are created only when you start the split.
web.splitWizard.mode.chapters-per-episod: Each episode gathers the same number of chapters.
web.splitWizard.help.mode.chapters-per-e: Divides the file into episodes with the same number of chapters. It also works with discs that have a different number of chapters.
web.splitWizard.mode.pattern.text: You set how many chapters each episode has.
web.splitWizard.help.mode.pattern: Divides the file following the list of chapters for each episode, in the order you write it.
web.splitWizard.help.mode.chapters-each: Creates one file for each chapter of the disc.
web.splitWizard.mode.split-at.text: Cuts at the times you set.
web.splitWizard.help.mode.split-at: Cuts the file at the points you set: each point separates two consecutive files.
web.splitWizard.mode.ranges.text: Extracts only the parts you set.
web.splitWizard.help.mode.ranges: Creates one file for each part set with a start and an end. The rest of the file is left out.
web.splitWizard.mode.trim.text: Removes the start, the end or both.
web.splitWizard.help.mode.trim: Creates a single file that keeps the part between the two points you set.
web.splitWizard.mode.manual.text: Build the parts in the cut editor.
web.splitWizard.help.mode.manual: Prepares the files for the cut editor, where you build the parts of each file.
web.splitWizard.validation.sourceRequire: Choose the file or folder to split.
web.splitWizard.validation.sourceNotFoun: The path {0} cannot be reached: choose an existing one.
web.splitWizard.validation.extensionsReq: Enter at least one extension, for example mkv.
web.splitWizard.validation.modeRequired: Choose how to split the files.
web.splitWizard.validation.row.pattern: enter a number of chapters from 1 up.
web.splitWizard.validation.row.points: enter a time like 21:40 or a frame like f1234.
web.splitWizard.validation.row.ranges: enter start and end like 21:40 or f1234, with the end after the start; END means the end of the file.
web.splitWizard.validation.trimRequired: Set at least one of the two points.
web.splitWizard.validation.timeInvalid: Enter a time like 1:30 or 00:01:30, or a frame like f1234.
web.splitWizard.validation.trimOrder: The end point comes after the start point.
web.splitWizard.validation.outputIsFile: Choose a folder: this path is a file.
web.split.emptyDescription: Choose the files, how to divide them and where to save the parts.
web.split.gridEmpty: Files found by Prepare and review appear here.
web.splitMontage.reviewExportNote: The split starts after the plans are reviewed.
web.splitJoin.overwriteNote: Set it in the Destination step of Configure split.
web.splitMontage.showOutput: Shows the selected file already assembled
web.splitMontage.removeMarkHelp: Removes the marked range from the selected file
web.splitMontage.trimTimeHelp: Type the time (hh:mm:ss.mmm) or f followed by the frame number, then Enter
web.splitMontage.splitHelp: Splits the selected segment in two at the cursor (S)
web.splitMontage.outputDragHelp: Drag to change the file order
web.splitMontage.segmentDragHelp: Drag to reorder or move to another file; hold Alt to copy
web.splitMontage.startHereHelp: Moves the start of the selected segment to the cursor
web.splitMontage.endHereHelp: Moves the end of the selected segment to the cursor, shown frame included
web.splitMontage.previousSegmentHelp: Selects the previous segment in the file list
web.splitMontage.previousSegmentNeedsOne: Available when the list has a segment before the selected one
web.splitMontage.nextSegmentHelp: Selects the next segment in the file list
web.splitMontage.nextSegmentNeedsOne: Available when the list has a segment after the selected one
web.splitMontage.goToStartHelp: Moves the cursor to the first frame of the segment
web.splitMontage.goToEndHelp: Moves the cursor to the last frame of the segment
web.splitMontage.previousKeyframeHelp: Moves the cursor to the source keyframe before the displayed frame
web.splitMontage.previousKeyframeNone: Available when there is a keyframe before the displayed frame
web.splitMontage.nextKeyframeHelp: Moves the cursor to the source keyframe after the displayed frame
web.splitMontage.nextKeyframeNone: Available when there is a keyframe after the displayed frame
web.splitMontage.markInHelp: Marks the range start at the displayed frame (I)
web.splitMontage.markOutHelp: Marks the range end at the displayed frame, frame included (O)
web.splitMontage.joinHelp: Joins this segment with the next one, which starts where this one ends
web.splitMontage.newEmptyFileHelp: Creates an empty output file; drop a segment here to create the file already filled
web.splitMontage.timeline: Source timeline with the file segments
web.splitMontage.timelineHint: Click: move the cursor · drag on an empty area: select a range · click a bar: select the segment · drag the edges of the selected segment: adjust it · right click on a bar: segment actions · right click inside the range, in the audio or keyframe area: range actions
web.splitMontage.sourceHelp: Shows the source frame under the cursor
web.splitMontage.showOutputNeedsClips: Available when the selected file contains at least one segment
web.splitMontage.addSegmentHelp: Appends to the selected file a segment from the cursor to the end of the source
web.splitMontage.needsOutput: Available with a selected output file
web.splitMontage.splitNeedsCursor: Available with the cursor inside the selected segment, after its first frame
web.splitMontage.needsOtherOutput: Available with at least one other output file
web.splitMontage.newFileHereHelp: Creates a new file with this segment and the ones that follow it
web.splitMontage.newFileHereNeedsPreviou: Available from the second segment of the file
web.splitMontage.joinNeedsContiguous: Available only when the next segment starts where this one ends
web.splitMontage.snapNeedsConfiguration: Available with keyframe snap enabled in the configuration
web.splitMontage.mergeNextNeedsClips: Available when this file and the next one contain segments
web.splitMontage.removeMarkNeedsOverlap: Available when the range covers a segment of the selected file
